why:
visits every goal live in the arena with its status, taking a stateless function pointer (no `std::function`, no allocator). It exists because our goal callback cannot hand back an owning handle the way rclcpp_action's accepted callback does, so this is how a C++ or Rust user learns which goals are outstanding. rclcpp's nearest is `rcl_action_server_get_goal_handles`; see `c:action_server_get_goal_handles`.
